notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.

Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: rows a-e are bank 't', rows f-j are bank 'b'. The image is drawn with rows j-f in the upper half and e-a in the lower half, so the lower half is bank 't' and its power rails are tp (+) and tn (-).

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap with legs in columns 4 and 6. The image makes the legs in the same column the joined pair, since the orange wire is on column 4 and the pin 2 wire and resistor are on column 6. Side 1 is column 4 (1.l at 4b.f, 1.r at 4t.e) and side 2 is column 6 (2.l at 6b.f, 2.r at 6t.e).
Pin 2 (teal wire) goes to 6b.j. The 10k resistor goes from 6t.c to 9t.c. Both are on the same side as the button's column-6 pair, so the pull-down is on the input side as the tutorial describes.

The 5V supply goes from uno 5V (red wire) to tp.1, then from the + rail through the orange wire (tp.3 to 4t.c) to the button's other side, column 4. Ground goes from uno GND.2 (black wire) to tn.1, then through the short black wire (tn.7 to 9t.b) to the resistor's far end.
Rail hole numbers are counted along the rail from the left in the image, in groups of five, so they are approximate. The Uno GND pin is the second GND on the power header, taken as GND.2.
The LED on pin 13 is the Uno's built-in LED, so there is no external LED.
